definitions.explanation: Having no defects or weaknesses whatsoever. A four-character idiom emphasizing total completeness and lack of any flaw.

examples.japanese: {完全無欠|かんぜんむけつ}な{人間|にんげん}はいない。
{彼|かれ}は{完全無欠|かんぜんむけつ}のヒーローとして{描|えが}かれている。
examples.english: He is depicted as a flawless hero.

examples.japanese: {完全無欠|かんぜんむけつ}を{求|もと}めるあまり、いつまでも{作品|さくひん}を{完成|かんせい}させられない{人|ひと}もいる。
examples.english: Some people are so obsessed with perfection that they can never finish their work.

notes:
USAGE NOTES:
{完全無欠|かんぜんむけつ} is a {四字熟語|よじじゅくご} composed of {完全|かんぜん} (complete, perfect) and {無欠|むけつ} (without defect). It is often used with の as a modifier ({完全無欠|かんぜんむけつ}の) or with な as a na-adjective.

In practice, it is frequently used in the negative — pointing out that nothing is truly {完全無欠|かんぜんむけつ} — or to describe idealized fictional characters.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {完全無欠|かんぜんむけつ}な{人|ひと} (a perfect person)
- {完全無欠|かんぜんむけつ}のアリバイ (an airtight alibi)
- {完全無欠|かんぜんむけつ}を{目指|めざ}す (aim for perfection)

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
- {非|ひ}の{打|う}ちどころがない — "without any fault" (idiomatic)
- {完璧|かんぺき} — "perfect, flawless" (more common in everyday speech)
